input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message to my daughter, but it just won’t go through. I’m not very good with these things, so I’m hoping you can help me fix it.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

I see that my phone shows a poor signal and it says 2G at the top. The little data symbol is on, and my battery is at 80%. I haven’t tried making a call or using the internet yet—should I try that now?
Alright, I changed the network mode like you said, and now the top of my screen shows a strong signal and says 5G. What should I do next?
I just tried to send the picture message again, but it still won’t go through. It looks like my phone still can’t send MMS messages. What should I do now?

I checked my phone’s APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Is that what it’s supposed to be? I’m not sure what any of that means.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is turned off on my phone. What should I try next?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it has access to storage and phone, but I don’t see anything about SMS. Is that a problem? What should I do?
I went ahead and gave the messaging app permission for SMS, but I still can’t send picture messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t it working yet? Is there something else I should try?
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. I’m starting to worry—am I going to lose my photos or anything important if we keep trying things? What else can we do?

Yes, I think that would be best. I’m feeling a bit overwhelmed with all these steps, and I just want to make sure I don’t lose anything important on my phone. Please connect me with someone who can help me fix this. Thank you for your patience.

###TRANSFER###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

I see that my phone shows a poor signal and it says 2G at the top. The little data symbol is on, and my battery is at 80%. I haven’t tried making a call or using the internet yet—should I try that now?

Thank you for sharing those details. Since your phone is showing a 2G connection and a poor signal, that could be the reason why your picture messages aren’t going through. MMS usually requires at least a 3G or higher connection.

Let’s try to improve your connection first. Please change your phone’s network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, if available. On your phone, look for the option to change your “Network Mode” or “Preferred Network Type” and select “4G/5G Preferred” or “LTE/5G Preferred.”

Once you’ve done that, let me know if your signal improves or if you see “4G,” “LTE,” or “5G” at the top of your screen. If you need step-by-step instructions, just let me know your phone model and I can guide you through it!

Let me know if it goes through this time or if you still have trouble sending it. If it still doesn’t work, I’ll guide you through the next steps to fix the issue.

I just tried to send the picture message again, but it still won’t go through. It looks like my phone still can’t send MMS messages. What should I do now?

Could you please check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings and let me know if you see an MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL listed? If you’re not sure how to check, I can guide you through the steps for your phone model, or you can let me know what you see in the APN settings.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my phone’s APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Is that what it’s supposed to be? I’m not sure what any of that means.

Thank you for checking your APN settings and providing the details. The APN name and MMSC URL you listed look correct for most carriers, so that’s a good sign.

Next, let’s check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your phone, as sometimes this can interfere with sending MMS messages. Could you please check your phone’s settings and let me know if Wi-Fi Calling is turned on? If you’re not sure how to check, let me know your phone model and I can guide you through the steps.

Thank you for confirming that Wi-Fi Calling is off. Since your network and APN settings look correct, and Wi-Fi Calling is off, let’s check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS.

Please check your messaging app’s permissions and make sure it has access to both “Storage” and “SMS.” If you’re not sure how to check or change app permissions, let me know your phone model and I can guide you through the steps.

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it has access to storage and phone, but I don’t see anything about SMS. Is that a problem? What should I do?

Yes, your messaging app needs permission to access SMS in order to send and receive text and picture messages. Please go to your phone’s app settings, find your messaging app, and look for an option to enable or allow “SMS” permission. 

If you see an option to grant SMS permission, please enable it. After that, try sending the picture message again.

If you don’t see an option for SMS permission, let me know your phone model and I can provide step-by-step instructions.
